memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'To make artistic designs for work in gold, silver and bronze, to cut and set stones, to work in wood and to engage in all kinds of artistic crafts.'" - Exod 35:32-33 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"Artistic designs." "Artistic crafts." God's own Word uses this language about work He commissioned and empowered.

The tabernacle did not need to be beautiful in order to function. A plain tent would have kept out the sun. But God asked for beauty — colour, design, carefully cut stones, engraved wood — because beauty says something true about Him.

We serve a God who made a world He did not need to make lovely. Sunsets are not functionally necessary. Neither are birdsong, mountain ranges, or the colour of a pomegranate. Creation is beautiful because its Maker delights in beauty.

So art is not a spiritual luxury or a distraction from serious faith. Done well and offered rightly, it is worship. The musician, the writer, the designer, the person who takes trouble to make a home warm — none of this is beneath God's notice. He gave those instincts.

There is a caution: beauty can become an idol, admired for itself and detached from the God it points to. The tabernacle's beauty was always ordered toward His presence, never a substitute for it.

Whatever you make, make it well. Then hand it to Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you see beauty and creativity as gifts from God?
2. Is there creative work you have set aside that God might want you to take up?
3. Does the beauty in your life point you to God or away from Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Creator God, thank You for beauty and for the ability to make things. Let whatever I create point back to You. Amen.
